full_judgment: 51. The learned Deputy-Attorney-General Mr Farhad Ahmed cited the decision of the case of Sree Nitai Chandra Mandai vs State, reported in 5 MLR (SC) 339 and some other decisions and contends that the trial Court clearly found that there was no ocular evidence in this case but the prosecution proved the case on circumstantial evidence. The chain of circumstances clearly proved the case and the trial Court rightly awarded the punishment against the accused-persons and he prays for acceptance of the reference. The learned Deputy-Attorney-General in support of his submissions referred the decisions in the case of Sree Nitai Chandra Mandai vs State, reported in 5 MLR (SC) 339, Nazra vs State reported in 12 DLR 34, Nuruddin alias Shahbuddin vs State reported in 2005 BCR 98, Anisur Raman vs State reported in BCR 1987 (AD) 157, Md Badrul Hoque Chowdhury vs State reported in 18 BLD(AD) 85, Md Rezaul Haque vs State reported in 16 BLD (AD) 261, State vs Moslem reported in 55 DLR (2003) 117, Billal vs State reported in 52 DLR (AD) 143, State vs Md Eraj Meah reported in 9 BLC (2004) 571.
